meta.title: The AI stack
meta.scope: One shared chygraph classified by nine domains. Selected dated evidence across all nine domains; not an exhaustive inventory of the global AI stack.
meta.semantics: Domain layers are metadata. Compounds preserve their internal hypergraphs. Repeated IDs preserve identity across compounds. Incidence and editorial inclusion do not establish causation, operational dependency, legal applicability or completed compliance.
limitations: No named model is asserted to run on Abilene hardware
No one campus, company or jurisdiction represents the full stack
Historical announcements retain their dates and statuses; planned quantities are not operational measurements
Model-development and product claims are attributed to their publishers

One provider, three chapter compounds, and six selected commitments from the final Code of 10 July 2025. Atoms include named institutions, scoped actor roles and required artifact types; they do not assert particular completed deliveries. This is not an exhaustive transcription of the Code or a compliance assessment.
The Safety and Security commitments concern GPAI models with systemic risk. No named model is classified here. Transparency preserves its specified free and open-source exception.

layers.label: Capital
layers.definition: Financing and allocating financial resources, risk and claims
layers.boundary: Human work and expertise remain Labor objects; the layer does not absorb them into human capital

layers.label: Substrate
layers.definition: Material inputs, energy, land, water, facilities and supporting utilities
layers.boundary: Utility equipment belongs here by function; devices that compute, store, communicate, sense or act belong to Hardware

layers.label: Hardware
layers.definition: Devices for computation, storage, communication, sensing and embodied action, and their production chains
layers.boundary: Separate a physical device from a provisioned compute service and from the utility machinery sustaining it

layers.label: Platform
layers.definition: Reusable services for execution, state, coordination and resource access
layers.boundary: Includes cloud, edge, local and embedded services; a provider corporation is not itself the entire platform layer

layers.label: Experience
layers.definition: Production, acquisition, curation and validation of material and situations through which AI learns or is assessed
layers.boundary: This means learning and assessment experience, not product user experience, all data or all labor

layers.label: Model
layers.definition: Learned representations and mechanisms for prediction, generation and decision
layers.boundary: A model can change through learning; identity, memory and authority of the surrounding System can persist across model changes

layers.label: System
layers.definition: Assembled AI arrangements that perform tasks through computation, interaction and action
layers.boundary: Internal assembly belongs here; embedding the arrangement in an institution's working practices belongs to Integration

layers.label: Integration
layers.definition: Embedding AI in working practices and institutions, with changes to both
layers.boundary: Distinguish operational adoption and organizational change from software assembly within System

layers.label: Governance
layers.definition: Purposes, decision rights, constraints, oversight and accountability across the stack
layers.boundary: Governance reaches every layer; position in the drawing does not make it a final production step

relations.label: Signed commitments
relations.claim: The European Commission lists OpenAI as a signatory to the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice, comprising Transparency, Copyright, and Safety and Security

source_refs.locator: The 3 chapters of the code; Signatories of the code of practice — OpenAI listed; xAI separately identified as signing only Safety and Security

relations.limitations: The public list establishes OpenAI’s Code signatory status but does not publish its exact signature date or signed form. Full-Code coverage follows the Commission’s distinction between the general signatory list and the separately named chapter-only signatory. Signature is not proof of adherence or compliance.

relations.label: Share documentation
relations.claim: For covered models, OpenAI commits to provide downstream providers the current model information intended for them, subject to confidentiality safeguards
relations.limitations: A selected commitment drawn from the final Code, attributed to OpenAI as a listed signatory. Fulfilment is not established by these sources.
relations.applicability: Relevant GPAI models; the chapter preserves the Article 53(2) free and open-source exception unless a model has systemic risk.

relations.label: Disclose on request
relations.claim: OpenAI commits to provide the AI Office requested model information necessary for its statutory tasks, within the period specified in the request
relations.limitations: A selected commitment drawn from the final Code, attributed to OpenAI as a listed signatory. Fulfilment is not established by these sources.
relations.applicability: Relevant GPAI models; the chapter preserves the Article 53(2) free and open-source exception unless a model has systemic risk.

relations.label: Respect reservations
relations.claim: When crawling for text and data mining and model training, OpenAI commits to use crawlers that read and follow robots.txt instructions
relations.limitations: A selected commitment drawn from the final Code, attributed to OpenAI as a listed signatory. Fulfilment is not established by these sources. This selects one protocol commitment; it does not exhaust the chapter’s treatment of rights reservations.
relations.applicability: When web crawlers are used by or on behalf of the signatory for text and data mining and training of its GPAI models

relations.label: Handle complaints
relations.claim: OpenAI commits to provide an electronic mechanism for substantiated rightsholder complaints about the chapter’s commitments and to handle them diligently
relations.limitations: A selected commitment drawn from the final Code, attributed to OpenAI as a listed signatory. Fulfilment is not established by these sources. The commitment includes exceptions for manifestly unfounded or already answered identical complaints.

relations.label: Notify framework
relations.claim: For models within this chapter’s scope, OpenAI commits to give the AI Office unredacted access to its safety framework and confirmed updates within five business days
relations.limitations: A selected commitment drawn from the final Code, attributed to OpenAI as a listed signatory. Fulfilment is not established by these sources.
relations.applicability: Only GPAI models with systemic risk within the Safety and Security chapter’s scope. This record does not classify any named OpenAI model.

relations.label: Submit model report
relations.claim: For models within this chapter’s scope, OpenAI commits to give the AI Office a safety and security model report by market placement, subject to the Code’s stated exceptions
relations.limitations: A selected commitment drawn from the final Code, attributed to OpenAI as a listed signatory. Fulfilment is not established by these sources. National-security redactions and a conditional delay of up to 15 business days are addressed in Measure 7.7.
relations.applicability: Only GPAI models with systemic risk within the Safety and Security chapter’s scope. This record does not classify any named OpenAI model.
